title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Diabetic ketoacidosis

Vitals:
T: 98.2 F, HR: 88, RR: 18, BP: 132/84, SpO2: 97% on RA.

Recent Labs:
Glucose: 450 mg/dL (admission), 140 mg/dL (discharge)
Bicarb: 12 mEq/L (admission), 22 mEq/L (discharge)
Anion Gap: 18 (admission), 10 (discharge)
Ketones: Positive (admission), Negative (discharge)
HbA1c: 9.4%
eGFR: 72 mL/min

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Fatigue, polyuria.
Respiratory: NAD.
CV: No chest pain.
GI: Nausea reported on admission.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.

Social History:
Lives with daughter. Retired. Non-smoker.

Family History:
Mother: Type 1 diabetes.
Father: Hypertension.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 80-year-old female with a known hx of type 1 diabetes. Presented to ED with altered mental status and fruity breath. Labs confirmed DKA. Pt admitted for stabilization. Initiated aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and continuous insulin drip. Managed for metabolic derangements. Pt responded well to treatment. Bicarb normalized, ketones cleared, and glucose stabilized. Pt tolerated oral intake well before discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Diabetic ketoacidosis
2. Type 1 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
1. Insulin Lispro: 10 units subcutaneous before meals
2. Insulin Glargine: 20 units subcutaneous at bedtime
3. Metformin: 500 mg BID

Follow-up:
F/u with primary care physician in 1 week for labs and insulin titration. Pt instructed to call if severe symptoms return.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Type 1 diabetes with ketoacidosis without coma: E10.10 (HCC 36).
